#### What type of PR is this?
/kind failing-test

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This PR adds AzureFile e2e tests for csi migration.
Actually we already have e2e tests which could test against in-tree and Azure File csi driver: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/azurefile-csi-driver/tree/master/test/e2e, while we still need to add e2e tests in k/k

<details>

issue_context.title: Missing Azure File e2e tests
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

Azure File is one of the intree storage plugins available in k8s, however, we currently don't have a e2e tests for it.

Having such tests would be helpful to test CSI migration for Azure File.

### What did you expect to happen?

Azure File e2e tests should run on Azure.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Just run the storage e2e test suite on an Azure cluster.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

1.23


### Cloud provider

Azure

### OS version

_No response_

### Install tools

_No response_

### Container runtime (CRI) and and version (if applicable)

_No response_

### Related plugins (CNI, CSI, ...) and versions (if applicable)

_No response_

We are migrating all the cloud provider related tests to cloud-provider specific CI. So I think azurefile e2e test should be running on cloud-provider-azure or azurefile-csi-driver.

actually you could run azure file e2e tests by, it's not in k/k repo:
```console
/test pull-kubernetes-e2e-aks-engine-azure-file-windows-conainerd
/test pull-kubernetes-e2e-aks-engine-azure-file-windows-dockershim
/test pull-kubernetes-e2e-capz-azure-file
/test pull-kubernetes-e2e-capz-azure-file-vmss
```

@Jiawei0227 I agree these jobs should be running on Azure-specific CI. However, the intree plugin code lives in kubernetes/kubernetes, so IMO the code for the tests should be hosted in the same code base.

@andyzhangx I believe those tests jobs you listed don't run the k/k test suite, they seem to run a different testsuite specific to Azure. As far as I know, one of the requirements for CSI migration is to run the k/k test suite.

@andyzhangx running k/k tests is really a prerequisite for CSI migration GA, it covers Kubernetes features pretty well and we already caught couple of issues there.

Last example: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/vsphere-csi-driver/issues/1600
(vSphere does not have a public CI, but at least I can run the tests manually)

@jsafrane actually there are already k/k e2e tests testing against azure file csi driver: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/azurefile-csi-driver/blob/master/test/external-e2e/run.sh#L27-L38, so if could be we change the provisioner to in-tree driver, those tests should test against csi migration also.

Check how Azure Disk in-tree volume tests are set up in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5b1e5387591dd3ad0b3ddacc9e44a6ac7260078e/test/e2e/storage/drivers/in_tree.go#L1541. The hardest part is `CreateVolume()`, that allows for testing in-line and pre-provisioned volumes and at the same time it needs to talk to the cloud outside of Kubernetes.

review_comments:
I think this will lead to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fa537c3a3b156ff431fd99348a7464876e5a5a64/test/e2e/framework/providers/azure/azure.go#L66

And it will create Azure Disk, not Azure File. There is IMO only one CreatePD per cloud provider and it creates ~AzureFile~ Azure Disk. IMO you could add `CreateShare` in the cloud provider and call it directly from here (with some retry).
